spec_features.evidence: loop.py: error -> break (110-113), tests_passed -> solved/break (145-150), finish -> break (152-155), free-text give-up -> `finished_reason='gave_up'` break (160-162), max_turns via for/else (171-172). All branches actually break the loop.

spec_features.evidence: loop.py:157-169: when `not assistant_msg.tool_calls`, the code only appends a nudge USER message; there is NO consecutive-no-op counter and NO break for repeated no-ops. The comment at 157-158 says 'if it keeps doing so, treat as a stall and end the run' but no code path enforces it — a model emitting no tool calls indefinitely is only nudged each turn until max_turns. Only an explicit give-up phrase (160-162) breaks early.
spec_features.notes: Claim exists solely in the comment; no implementation. Persistent no-ops do not end the run, they fall through to the max_turns cap.
